description:
Requests a page and reports whether it answered, how long it took, the full redirect chain
it went through, whether plain HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS, and which security headers came
back.

Use it to answer "is this site up?", "why does this URL take four redirects to load?",
"does http:// still work and should it?" or "does this site send HSTS?". It is the check
to run when a client reports that a page is down or slow.

Do not use it to inspect a certificate — that is ssl_check — or for registration and DNS,
which is domain_check. It fetches one page, not a whole site: use seo_audit for crawling.

Redirects are followed one hop at a time so the whole chain is visible, up to ten hops.
Response time is wall clock to the first response headers and includes DNS, TCP and TLS
setup, so it is not a measure of server processing time.

Status codes are graded rather than lumped together: 5xx, 404 and 410 are critical, 401
and 403 are a warning because they are normal for a staging site, and 429 is reported as
unknown because a throttled check establishes nothing about real availability. A
certificate browsers refuse (expired, not yet valid, revoked, for another host,
self-signed) is critical, since visitors cannot open the site; a timeout, a DNS failure
or a handshake that ended in an alert is an error, since a firewall blocking this server
or a proxy on its side looks the same from here. Returns findings
ordered by urgency, worst first.

url.description: The page to request, e.g. "https://example.com". A bare domain such as "example.com" is accepted and tried over HTTPS. Include the path when a specific page matters; the homepage is checked otherwise. Only http and https URLs are accepted.

name: uptime_check

checkedAt.description: When the check ran, ISO 8601 in UTC.

items.description: One actionable observation about the target.

code.description: Stable identifier for this kind of observation, e.g. "cert_expires_soon".

message.description: One sentence explaining the observation in plain words.

severity.description: How much attention this needs. "critical" means act now; "warning" means act this month; "unknown" means the check could not establish the fact, which is not the same as it being fine.

hsts.description: The HSTS policy, read from the HTTPS response only.

activelyDisabled.description: True when max-age=0, which deletes an existing policy rather than weakening it.

preload.description: Whether the preload directive is set.

preloadEligible.description: Whether the policy would meet the preload list requirements. Informational only — preload is an opt-in commitment and its absence is never reported as a problem.

present.description: Whether Strict-Transport-Security was sent over HTTPS.

https.description: Whether visitors arriving over plain HTTP are moved to HTTPS.

probedHttp.description: Whether plain HTTP was probed for an upgrade.

upgradeOnFirstHop.description: Whether the very first HTTP response redirects to HTTPS.

upgradesToHttps.description: Whether plain HTTP eventually reaches HTTPS.

reachable.description: Whether the server answered at all.

redirects.description: The redirect chain, followed manually one hop at a time.

brokenAt.description: The URL the chain redirected to and could not reach, or null when it ended normally. When this is set, finalUrl is where the chain stopped, not where it meant to go.

crossHost.description: Whether the chain ended on a different host than it started.

elapsedMs.description: Wall-clock milliseconds for this hop alone.

location.description: The Location header, or null when this was the destination.

url.description: The URL requested at this hop.

loopDetected.description: Whether the chain revisited a URL it had already requested.

truncated.description: Whether the chain hit the hop limit before ending.

responseTimeMs.description: Wall-clock milliseconds to the first response headers. Includes DNS, TCP and TLS setup, so it is not server processing time.

contentSecurityPolicyReportOnly.description: True when the only policy present is report-only, which enforces nothing.

deadHeadersPresent.description: Headers present but inert in every current browser. Worth removing, never worth adding.

framingProtection.description: Which mechanism actually prevents the page being framed.

permissionsPolicy.description: Acted on by Chromium browsers only.

severity.description: How much attention this needs. "critical" means act now; "warning" means act this month; "unknown" means the check could not establish the fact, which is not the same as it being fine.

status.description: Status code at the end of the redirect chain.

url.description: The URL that was requested first.

title: Site reachability and headers
